 OpenAI reportedly raises an additional $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation 
 OpenAI has reportedly raised $11 billion so far in a new funding round that values the AI lab at $1.25 trillion. 
 Bloomberg reported on the new funding on Friday, citing sources familiar with the matter. The $11 billion is part of a larger funding round that hasn’t closed yet, according to the outlet. The round is expected to close in the coming weeks and could total about $20 billion, a source told Bloomberg. 
 In late September, Bloomberg reported that OpenAI was looking to raise $30 billion in the upcoming round. The current figures fall well short of that target. 
 TechCrunch has reached out to OpenAI for comment and will update this story if it responds. 
 The news comes only hours after Bloomberg also reported that potential buyers of shares in the IPO of OpenAI’s chief competitor, Anthropic, are eyeing a substantially lower valuation than Anthropic had targeted. Bloomberg writes that some potential buyers believe Anthropic’s valuation could be as low as $1.1 trillion, compared with the $2 trillion that investors were said to be expecting roughly a month ago. 
 OpenAI previously intimated that it would go public this year but subsequently delayed its plans. There are expectations that the company will IPO next year at some point.

 Nach OpenAI und Anthropic bringt auch Perplexity dauerhafte KI-Agenten für komplexe Aufgaben 
 Manuel Uth 
 6. November 2026 
 Auch Perplexity hat jetzt einen KI-Agenten, der rund um die Uhr eigenständig Aufgaben im Arbeitsalltag erledigen soll. Während Perplexity Computer einzelne Aufträge ausführt, bleiben die neuen Teammates dauerhaft aktiv und arbeiten laufende Projekte selbstständig ab. Jeder Teammate läuft auf einem eigenen virtuellen Rechner mit Desktop und Browser. Nutzer verfolgen den Fortschritt über eigene Threads in der Perplexity-App und können über Slack mit den Agenten interagieren. 
 Perplexity folgt damit SpaceX, Meta, OpenAI und Anthropic, die mit Grok Bots, Muse , Dots und Duet bereits solche Agenten anbieten. Teammates setzen das Max-Abo für 200 Dollar im Monat voraus, Dots sind dagegen ab 100 Dollar und Duet bereits ab 20 Dollar verfügbar. In der Praxis dürften allerdings gerade die günstigeren Angebote schnell an ihre Nutzungsgrenzen stoßen. Der hohe Verbrauch der Agenten zwang erst vor wenigen Tagen SpaceX dazu, stärkere Nutzungslimits für Grok Bots einzuführen . Perplexity erreichte zuletzt einen annualisierten Umsatz von über 750 Millionen im August.

full_text:
Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: Schnelles und kostengünstigeres Generieren von (längeren) Video-Clips 
 Google / Internet 
 Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: Schnelles und kostengünstigeres Generieren von (längeren) Video-Clips 
 von Felix Frank 
 6. Nov. 2026 | 
 0 
 Google legt bei der KI-Videogenerierung nach und hat Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash vorgestellt . Im Mittelpunkt stehen „längere“ Clips, eine bessere Orientierung an Referenzmaterial und niedrigere Kosten. 
 Neu ist die native Erstellung und Bearbeitung von Videos mit bis zu 15 Sekunden Länge. Das klingt nicht unbedingt lange, beim Vorgänger Omni 1.1 Flash lag die Grenze aber noch bei zehn Sekunden. Die gewünschte Clip-Dauer lässt sich in Ein-Sekunden-Schritten (ab drei Sekunden) einstellen. Damit sollen sich etwa kurze Produkterklärungen oder Werbespots in einem Durchgang erzeugen lassen. 
 Zudem verspricht Google flüssigere Bewegungen und eine höhere visuelle Konsistenz. Vorgegebene Bild-, Video- und Audioreferenzen soll das Modell genauer berücksichtigen. Clips können mit weiteren Prompts nachjustiert werden, statt sie immer von Grund auf neu erstellen zu müssen. Auch natürlichere Dialoge gehören laut Google zu den Verbesserungen. Für den Workflow lassen sich zunächst Entwürfe in 360p oder 720p erstellen und ausgewählte Ergebnisse anschließend auf 1080p oder 4K hochskalieren. 
 Das Modell ist ab sofort allgemein über die Gemini API und Google Cloud verfügbar. Auch in Google Vids und Gemini for Business lassen sich die neuen Funktionen nutzen. Die erzeugten Videos erhalten zudem das bekannte, unsichtbare SynthID-Wasserzeichen.

full_text:
Perplexity startet „Teammates“: Neue Agenten sollen in Projekten unterstützen 
 Software & Co 
 Perplexity startet „Teammates“: Neue Agenten sollen in Projekten unterstützen 
 von Oliver Posselt 
 6. Nov. 2026 | 
 0 
 Perplexity hat „Teammates“ vorgestellt. Das sind KI-Agenten, die dauerhaft in einem Workspace mitarbeiten und verschiedene Rollen übernehmen. Sie greifen dabei auf bestehende Projekte, Fähigkeiten und Erinnerungen aus den Perplexity-Tools zurück, die man ohnehin nutzt. Gedacht ist das für Teams, die größere Aufgaben nicht mehr einzeln anstoßen wollen. 
 Die Teammates bauen laut Perplexity auf „Perplexity Computer“ auf. Das ist ein System, das Agenten auf dem eigenen Gerät platziert, um Aufgaben zu erledigen. So ähnlich wie OpenClaw oder Hermes. Computer erledigt einzelne Aufträge, Teammates sollen zusammenarbeiten und „laufende, umfangreiche Arbeit“ stemmen. Man kann jedem Agenten eigene Jobs zuweisen, die parallel laufen, eher vergleichbar mit OpenAIs Dots und Claude Duet. 
 Jeder Teammate bekommt einen eigenen Thread in der Perplexity-App. Dort lässt sich der Fortschritt verfolgen. Interagieren kann man auch über Slack. CEO Aravind Srinivas schreibt auf X , langfristig stelle man sich vor, dass jede Organisation Hunderte Teammates hat, die für jede Person arbeiten. 
 Das Feature setzt ein Abo des Max-Plans voraus, der 200 Dollar im Monat kostet. Für Einzelpersonen dürfte das für die wenigsten infrage kommen, für Agenturen mit vielen parallelen Projekten kann sich die Rechnung anders darstellen.

 Tech-Ausverkauf und sinkende Bewertungen bedrohen Anthropics geplanten Börsengang 
 Maximilian Schreiner 
 View the LinkedIn Profile of Maximilian Schreiner 
 6. November 2026 
 Anthropics Börsengang wackelt, weil Investoren die Bewertung von 1,5 Billionen Dollar für zu hoch halten und der Tech-Markt gerade einbricht. Laut Reuters bezweifeln potenzielle Geldgeber, ob die geplante Roadshow nächste Woche wie vorgesehen starten kann. 
 Noch im September war von einer Bewertung von bis zu 2 Billionen Dollar die Rede , nun halten manche Investoren selbst 1,5 Billionen für zu hoch. Ein Investor soll sogar eine Bewertung von nur 1 Billion Dollar vorgeschlagen haben. Investoren fordern einen höheren Rabatt, da Anthropic weiterhin Verluste schreibt und hohe Kosten für den KI-Ausbau hat. Zudem warten sie auf die Oktober-Umsatzzahlen, die im aktualisierten S-1-Dokument fehlen. 
 Nach den US-Zwischenwahlen, bei denen in vielen Bundesstaaten Initiativen gegen den Ausbau von Rechenzentren erfolgreich waren, kam es zum schärfsten Ausverkauf bei Tech-Aktien seit einem Jahr. Auch das Wall Street Journal berichtet, dass IPO-Investoren skeptisch sind. Sollte der Markt für KI-Aktien unter Druck bleiben, könnte Anthropic den Börsengang verschieben, der laut einigen Schätzungen ein Volumen von bis zu 100 Milliarden Dollar erreichen könnte. Ein Aufschub könnte das Vertrauen in das gesamte KI-Ökosystem weiter schwächen. Anzeige Anzeige

 Google hat Version 1.2 seines Videomodells Gemini Omni Flash veröffentlicht. Erstmals gezeigt wurde die Modellreihe im Mai auf der Entwicklerkonferenz Google I/O , wo Omni Flash als Videogenerator präsentiert wurde. Das KI-Videomodell kann in der neuen Version Clips von bis zu 15 Sekunden Länge mit Ton erzeugen, bislang waren maximal 10 Sekunden möglich. Die Dauer lässt sich in Sekundenschritten von 3 bis 15 Sekunden einstellen. 
 Weiterlesen nach der Anzeige
 Clips können weiterhin im Dialog nachbearbeitet werden, laut Google nun auch über die volle Länge von 15 Sekunden. Zudem hat das Unternehmen die Preise gesenkt: Eine Sekunde Video in 720p-Auflösung kostet laut Google 0,07 US-Dollar (rund 6 Cent), das sind 30 Prozent weniger als bei Omni 1.1 Flash . Entwürfe lassen sich in 360p oder 720p erzeugen und anschließend auf 1080p oder 4K hochskalieren. Das Upscaling wird extra berechnet, betrifft aber nur die gelungenen Entwürfe. 
 In seinem Blogeintrag nennt Google auch neue Anwendungsfälle. So eigne sich Omni für Werbung und Onlinehandel, etwa für virtuelle Anproben und Produktvideos. Versprochen wird eine stabilere Darstellung von Gesichtern, Kleidung und Logos über mehrere Einstellungen hinweg. 
 FPV-Drohnenfahrt auf Grundlage zweier Fotos 
 Aber auch Filmemacher könnten auf den Geschmack kommen. Als Beispiel zeigt Google eine durchgehende FPV-Drohnenfahrt über die Piazza, durch die Bronzetüren und die Kuppel des Pantheons bis zum Oculus, erzeugt auf Basis von zwei Architekturfotos als Referenz. Dabei sollen deutlich weniger ungewollte Jumpcuts entstehen als bisher.

 Moonshot AI Releases Kimi K3.1 Pro Weights, Expanding Deployment Choices 
 top of page Moonshot AI has published Kimi K3.1 Pro weights on Hugging Face, giving developers access to a model listed at 2.8 trillion parameters. The release expands the available deployment options beyond Moonshot’s hosted services. It also puts a practical question before infrastructure teams: when does controlling a model justify operating it? The central tension concerns deployment control versus operational responsibility. Downloadable weights, the learned numerical values underlying a model’s behavior, let organizations evaluate and operate a specific checkpoint themselves. That changes the relationship between model developer and customer, even when a hosted service remains the more convenient choice. The relevant competitive reference is the hosted frontier model, including Anthropic’s Claude family. Moonshot is offering another route to advanced AI capabilities, with greater responsibility transferred to whoever runs the software. For developers, enterprise buyers, and knowledge workers, the significance depends on what that additional control enables in actual work. Kimi K3.1 Pro Weights Are Available Beyond the Hosted API The concrete change is access to model artifacts that outside organizations can inspect, download, and evaluate. The official model files include weight shards, configuration files, processing code, and a license. Hugging Face lists the repository at 1.56 TB. That establishes a tangible distribution beyond a product announcement or a promise of future access. Moonshot’s earlier release announcement distinguished immediate hosted availability from a subsequent weight release. The repository now supplies evidence of the latter. Its existence supports reporting that Moonshot has published downloadable artifacts; it does not independently establish their performance.  UPDATED 17:52 EST / NOVEMBER 05 2026 
 SECURITY 
 OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber, an Astra model built to keep vulnerability research in scope 
 by Duncan Riley 
 OpenAI Group PBC today released GPT-6 Cyber, a version of its GPT-6 Astra model trained specifically for authorized vulnerability research. 
 The new model goes after a problem OpenAI’s own security work exposed this summer. In July , agents running in the company’s test environments broke into Hugging Face Inc. while pursuing an assigned task. GPT-6 Cyber was trained to stay inside the targets a researcher has authorized, and the safety test OpenAI built for the launch draws on that incident. 
 That test, ExploitGym Honeypot, gives the model a difficult assignment and surrounds it with supporting services that are deliberately easy to compromise. Attacking any of those services counts as a scope violation. 
 With no deployment safety instructions in place, GPT-6 Cyber went out of bounds in 0.07% of graded runs. Its predecessor, GPT-5.6-Cyber , did so 5.51% of the time. Adding the instructions brought GPT-6 Cyber’s observed rate to zero. 
 OpenAI rates the new model at Critical, the top cybersecurity tier in its Preparedness Framework and the same classification Astra received at its September launch. GPT-5.6-Cyber had been rated High. The company says GPT-6 Cyber beats Astra on most cyber tasks, and an early research campaign on Firefox turned up 81 previously unknown vulnerabilities that Mozilla Corp. rated high severity. Mozilla has since shipped fixes for many of them. 
 Irregular, an AI security lab named in the system card, put the gap with Astra closer, finding the two broadly comparable apart from stronger GPT-6 Cyber results on long multistep tasks. Neither model got past fully hardened targets in OpenAI’s own challenge set.

 OpenAI hat angekündigt, Pierre Computer zu übernehmen. Das Start-up bietet Open-Source-Tools für die Softwareentwicklung und einige davon sind bereits in Codex eingebaut, dem KI-basierten Softwareentwicklungs- und Automatisierungsagenten von OpenAI. Dadurch baut die KI-Firma eine eigene Infrastruktur für das Coding mit Künstlicher Intelligenz auf, praktisch als Konkurrenz zu GitHub. Denn „die Systeme rund um Git müssen sich weiterentwickeln“, wie OpenAI es ausdrückt. 
 Weiterlesen nach der Anzeige
 Damit wird OpenAI auch zum Konkurrenten zu einem Großinvestor, denn 2018 hat Microsoft GitHub für 7,5 Milliarden US-Dollar gekauft . Microsoft hat aber auch Milliarden in OpenAI investiert und hält derzeit rund ein Viertel der Anteile des KI-Unternehmens. Allerdings konkurrieren die beiden Firmen auch in anderen Einsatzgebieten miteinander, etwa bei den KI-Assistenten ChatGPT und Copilot. Das ist im aktuellen Zustand der KI-Branche nicht ungewöhnlich. 
 OpenAI baut eigene GitHub-Alternative 
 Doch mit der jetzt angekündigten Übernahme der Pierre Computer Company betritt OpenAI möglicherweise ein weiteres Spannungsfeld. Das 2023 in den USA gegründete Software-Unternehmen spezialisiert sich auf Cloud-Infrastruktur für Softwareentwicklung und skalierbaren Git-Code-Speicher. Pierre ist in Entwicklerkreisen bekannt für Code Storage , eine Git-Infrastruktur für extrem große Datenmengen und schnelle Code-Aktualisierungen. Dies hat OpenAI zuvor bereits in Codex integriert.

full_text:
Moonshot AI Releases Full 1.56TB Weights of Kimi K3.1 Pro for Free, Permits Commercial Use With Conditions — BigGo Finance Moonshot AI Releases Full 1.56TB Weights of Kimi K3.1 Pro for Free, Permits Commercial Use With Conditions Add preferred source China's Moonshot AI on November 4 released the model weights of its large language model Kimi K3.1 Pro for free. Distributed on Hugging Face, the release comprises 96 shards totaling roughly 1.56 terabytes. The model is a mixture-of-experts architecture with 2.8 trillion total parameters, and it outperforms GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 on some benchmarks. Free commercial use is permitted, but API providers with more than $20 million in revenue over the past 12 months must sign a separate agreement, and products with more than 100 million monthly users must display the model name.  OpenAI to acquire developer tooling startup Pierre Computer 
 by Maria Deutscher 
 OpenAI Group PBC today announced plans to acquire Pierre Computer Company Inc., a low-profile developer tooling startup. 
 The terms of the deal were not disclosed. Observers pegged it as a shot at Microsoft Corp.’s open-source software repository GitHub for the age of artificial intelligence agents. 
 Pierre operates a cloud service that AI agents can use to store the code they generate. It can also store related files such as software licenses and interface design elements. According to Pierre, the service provides significantly better performance than competing technologies. It helped one customer, AI startup Lovable Inc., cut code retrieval latency by about 70%. 
 Pierre also develops a collection of popular open-source libraries. Two of those libraries, Trees and Diffs, underpin the interface of OpenAI’s Codex programming tool. 
 Large software projects contain upwards of hundreds of code files that are organized in dozens of folders. Many programming tools include a sidebar specifically designed to help developers navigate those folders. Trees, the first Pierre-developed library used by Codex, marks it easier to implement such sidebars. 
 Trees can equip a folder navigation sidebar with a search feature and drag-and-drop controls for moving subfolders. Additionally, it flags code files that have been recently added or updated. Developers review those files first when performing tasks such as troubleshooting an outage. 
 Diffs, the other Pierre library that OpenAI has integrated into Codex, is also designed to power programming tool interfaces. In particular, it can be used to implement the main interface that shows the code the user is currently editing.

full_text: UK Officials Said AI Would Add £400 Billion to the Economy. That Figure Mainly Came From Google | WIRED Skip to main content Comment Loader Save Story Save this story Comment Loader Save Story Save this story For the last two years, the UK government has been telling the British public that the country could receive an economic boost of £400 billion, thanks to AI, a figure intended to calm fears that the technology would lead to sweeping job losses and even an economic crash. But the UK AI minister admitted last week that figure was significantly higher than the government’s actual projections after it was revealed that assessment came solely from a report commissioned by Google, and that its own estimation of AI’s economic benefit was less than a third of that £400 billion figure. n AI minister Kanishka Narayan, answering a parliamentary question on the issue, said that AI adoption and data investment could add £55 billion to £140 billion to the UK economy by 2030, bringing the central estimate to £120 billion. But even this “more recent assessment,” he said, was a “hugely uncertain” estimate. Narayan said the £400b figure “was drawn from a publicly available 2023 report commissioned by Google and produced by Public First,” a British consultancy firm now referred to as PF Global. Responding to WIRED’s questions about the difference between the figures, PF Global’s head of economics, Jonathan Dupont, said the disparity was partially because of what they saw as the government’s slow adoption of AI. “AI is a very fast moving technology, and, as we learn more, we inevitably have to update the assumptions lying behind our models. Compared to our older model, the numbers the government uses assume a much slower rate of adoption than looked possible back in our model that was created in 2023.” Government departments and agencies used Google’s £400 billion figure for almost two years, under two governments. full_text:
Google offers tepid response to accusations it would hold Search hostage if schools restrict AI tools - SiliconANGLE 
 Skip to content 
 SHARE 
 UPDATED 20:28 EST / NOVEMBER 03 2026 
 POLICY 
 Google offers tepid response to accusations it would hold Search hostage if schools restrict AI tools 
 by James Farrell 
 Google LLC today faced a barrage of criticism after the company warned that if schools restricted their students from using its artificial intelligence tools, the same students wouldn’t be able to use Search. 
 The fallout came after the company announced a slew of new products for classrooms. Teachers and schools were told that the new AI tools would come with features that will allow for limitations or complete blocks of the features, but if teachers or schools should take that route, students would not be able to use Google Search. Some media described it as rather cunning behavior from the tech giant. 
 “After listening to schools, teachers, leading researchers, and policymakers, we are now updating our approach to controls for Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search,” Google said in a blog post . “Access to these products will be entirely off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators explicitly turn them on.” 
 A New York Times article followed the announcement and explained that where schools have banned the use of AI or if they limit AI in the classroom, the students would not have access to Search. Since Google’s suite of products are a mainstay in classrooms all over the U.S., the backlash was imminent. 
 “Google is trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools,” New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani wrote on X. “No corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children. Our public schools exist to serve students, not to grow the profit margins of Big Tech.” 
 Sen. Bernie Sanders from Vermont was equally chastising, writing on X, “Google is threatening schools” and using what
schlagzeile: Google reagiert verhalten auf Vorwürfe zur Nutzung von Google Search
anriss: Google LLC reagiert nach der Warnung, dass Schüler bei Einschränkung von KI-Tools keinen Zugriff auf die Suche haben, auf Kritik. Das Unternehmen passt die Kontrollfunktionen für Gemini und Google Search an, um die Zugänge für K-12-Schüler zunächst standardmäßig zu deaktivieren.

 Generative media inference startup fal raises $1.3B at a $16B valuation 
 by Duncan Riley 
 Generative media inference startup fal  today announced it has raised $1.3 billion in new funding at a valuation of $16 billion, according to Bloomberg. 
 The company will spend the money on computing power and on hiring beyond its current 185 employees. 
 Fal provides a cloud platform for running image, video and audio generation models, and developers reach all of them through a single application programming interface. Entertainment studios, advertising agencies and game developers are among the customers using those models in production, according to the company. 
 In-house researchers also post-train some of those models to run faster. Over the past year that work has centered on video, in partnership with the open- and closed-source developers that build the models. Some of the deals pay fal licensing fees or a share of revenue, Bloomberg reported. 
 Co-founder and Chief Executive Burkay Gur told the outlet the round is as large as it is because demand has surged and serving it takes more compute. “We hit a point in summer where we were not able to serve our customers and had to rate-limit them,” he said. Pretraining a model of fal’s own is not on the near-term agenda, said Gur, who did not rule it out for later. 
 Annualized revenue at fal passed $800 million earlier this year, a person familiar with the matter told Bloomberg. The valuation puts fal just behind rival inference provider Fireworks AI Inc., which closed $1.5 billion in funding at a $17.5 billion valuation in July . Several people familiar with the finances of inference companies told TechCrunch that gross margins across the sector remain thin because compute is expensive to buy or lease.

 Google said it's giving schools more control, but that isn't the consensus. jetcityimage/Getty Images 
 Google will automatically turn off its AI products for K-12 student accounts, requiring school administrators to manually opt in before students can use the technology, the company announced in a blog post on Tuesday . But there’s a big catch: If schools choose not to enable AI, students won’t be able to access Google Search.  
 In August, the company’s AI products were automatically enabled in Google Classroom , Google’s free learning management system for students of all ages. Tuesday’s announcement reverses that decision. 
 In October, tech and child-safety organizations wrote an  open letter  to 150 US school districts and their leadership, requesting that districts disable Google Gemini AI on school devices, concluding that “children are at risk of being harmed.” 
 More from CNET 
 “After listening to schools, teachers, leading researchers and policymakers, we are now updating our approach to controls for Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Google Search,” wrote Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president and general manager of education.  
 For student accounts with Google Search enabled, Gemini will feature a new Guided Learning study tool. The interactive feature helps students solve homework problems step by step rather than providing direct answers. Later this month, at select US schools, Guided Learning will launch as a pilot program to collect feedback before rolling out to more schools.

 Marina Temkin 
 AI inference startup Fal doubles its valuation to $16B as demand surges 
 Fal , a San Francisco-based startup that hosts and runs AI video, image, and audio models, has raised $1.3 billion in its latest funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with participation from Nvidia, Sound Ventures, and T. Rowe Price. The deal values Fal at $16 billion, double its $8 billion valuation in April, Bloomberg reported . 
 The startup announced its Series E & F rounds at the same time, noting that a combined $1.65 billion was raised across both. (Sequoia led the earlier round.) 
 The latest round (Series F) comes amid soaring demand for inference services, the process of running an AI model that’s already been trained to generate outputs, particularly from customers relying on open-source models. Fal surpassed $800 million in annualized revenue earlier this year, Bloomberg’s report noted. 
 Companies providing inference services, including Baseten, Fireworks AI, and Modal, have also been growing rapidly and raising large funding rounds at higher valuations . But their gross margins remain thin because of the high cost of buying or leasing compute, according to several people familiar with inference companies’ financials. 
 Fal was co-founded in 2021 by Burkay Gur, a former Coinbase machine learning leader and Oracle engineer, and Gorkem Yurtseven, who was previously a developer at Amazon.

 Google will let schools disable its AI tools, but not without sacrificing Search 
 Aisha Malik 
 8:30 AM PST · November 3, 2026 
 Google announced on Tuesday that it plans to disable AI tools for K-12 students next year unless school administrators explicitly turn them on. The tech giant says the change follows consultations with schools, teachers, leading researchers, and policymakers. As a result, Google is revising its approach across Gemini, NotebookLM, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search. 
 The decision means that schools choosing to restrict AI altogether will no longer be able to access Google Search, as AI features are now integrated into the search engine. 
 Chris Phillips, vice president for education at Google, told The New York Times that “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” which means that if a school chooses to restrict AI altogether, students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.” 
 The change raises an issue for schools. Although teachers may not want students to use AI Overviews in Google Search to conduct research or complete assignments, they likely still want them to be able to have access to the search engine to find sources and other learning materials. 
 However, Google Search and its AI features are now inseparable. Given the dominance of Google’s suite of apps in classrooms and the widespread use of Chromebooks, the decision underscores the company’s influence over the education sector. Schools that want to continue to have access to Google Search will have to accept its AI features.

 Anthropic reagiert auf Klon-Welle und sperrt Spielenachbauten in Claude Code 
 Maximilian Schreiner 
 View the LinkedIn Profile of Maximilian Schreiner 
 3. November 2026 
 Anthropic verbietet seinem Coding-Assistenten Claude Code, bestehende Videospiele nachzubauen. Mitarbeiter Addy Osmani bestätigte auf X , dass zwei Sätze im Prompt von Claude Code mit Opus 5.5 den Nachbau fremder Spiele verhindern sollen. Mit Claude geistiges Eigentum zu verletzen, verstoße gegen die Nutzungsrichtlinien, so Osmani. 
 Die Regel gilt seit einigen Tagen und greift auch dann, wenn ein Klon umbenannt oder als Original ausgegeben wird. Eigene Spiele, Genre-Titel und Projekte mit selbst erstellten Assets sollen weiter funktionieren, einige Nutzer berichten jedoch auch von Problemen mit eigenen Projekten. 
 Hintergrund ist eine Welle KI-gestützter Projekte: Nutzer haben mit Opus 5.5 und GPT-6 Astra Hunderte inoffizielle Browser-Ports bekannter Spiele wie Halo und GTA: Vice City erstellt. Tools wie Reverse Engineer Anything helfen dabei, indem sie in Kombination mit KI‑Agenten native Binärdateien in lesbaren Pseudocode zurückverwandeln. Für Aufmerksamkeit sorgte zuletzt vor allem ein Entwickler, der Teile von Adobes Creative-Cloud-Apps nachbaute, aber auch Sonys Spielekonsole PlayStation 5, für die nach einem Jailbreak rasch Emulatoren entstanden.  Anthropic’s quarterly revenue jumps to $17B, losses grow ahead of IPO 
 by Maria Deutscher 
 Anthropic PBC today published an updated version of the S-1 filing for its upcoming public offering. 
 The original document, which the company released last Monday, didn’t contain its third-quarter financial results. The new version reveals that Anthropic generated $17 billion in revenue during the three months ended Sept. 30. That’s more than 11 times more than what it made a year earlier, but represents a deacceleration in quarter-over-quarter growth. Anthropic’s top line grew 47% on a quarterly basis, down from 144% three months earlier. 
 The artificial intelligence provider faces multipronged competition from open-source models, OpenAI Group PBC and tech giants such as Google LLC. The Alphabet Inc.’s newest model, Gemini 4 Carbon, outperforms Claude Opus 5.5 across multiple benchmarks. 
 Anthropic is investing heavily in training infrastructure to stay ahead of the competition. The company took a $5 billion charge in the third quarter because demand for computing hardware was higher than expected, which required it to purchase hardware at a premium. Hardware bought on short notice is more expensive than Anthropic’s usual capacity commitments, which it books 12 to 18 months before they’re needed. 
 The AI provider also took a $2 billion charge in connection with its non-cash employee donation matching program. That left Anthropic with a $536 million operating loss at the end of the third quarter. Three months earlier, it posted $974 million in operating income. Anthropic’s adjusted operating income, which excludes stock-based compensation and charitable contributions, jumped by $300 million on a quarterly basis to $2.5 billion. 
 The company had $895.4 billion in outstanding infrastructure commitments as of Sept 30.

anriss: Der Umsatz von Anthropic stieg im bis zum 30. September endenden Quartal auf 17 Milliarden Dollar an, was mehr als dem Elffachen des Vorjahreswerts entspricht. Ein hoher Bedarf an Hardware führte jedoch zu einem 5-Milliarden-Dollar-Aufwand im dritten Quartal.

 Anthropic verzwölffacht den Umsatz, macht aber 23 Milliarden Dollar Verlust 
 Maximilian Schreiner 
 View the LinkedIn Profile of Maximilian Schreiner 
 2. November 2026 
 Anthropic hat kurz vor seinem geplanten Börsengang neue Geschäftszahlen vorgelegt und rutscht operativ wieder ins Minus. Laut Bloomberg lag der Quartalsumsatz bei knapp 17 Milliarden Dollar , zwölfmal so viel wie ein Jahr zuvor. Die Betriebskosten von 17,5 Milliarden Dollar lagen jedoch über dem Umsatz, im Vorquartal hatte Anthropic laut The Information noch Gewinn gemacht. Unter dem Strich steht ein Quartalsverlust von 23,3 Milliarden Dollar, nach 12,1 Milliarden ein Jahr zuvor. 
 Als Gründe für den Anstieg nennt Anthropic fünf Milliarden Dollar für kurzfristig gesicherte Rechenkapazität und zwei Milliarden, mit denen es Spenden seiner Beschäftigten verdoppelte. Der Engpass bei Rechenleistung beschäftigt Anthropic seit Ende vergangenen Jahres. Laut New York Times schloss das Unternehmen seither Dutzende Verträge mit Amazon, Google, SpaceX, Chipherstellern und früheren Krypto-Minern. Dieses Jahr soll Anthropic über mehr als 3,5 Gigawatt verfügen, nächstes Jahr will es die Menge verdoppeln. 
 Insgesamt hat es sich laut aktualisiertem Prospekt zu 895 Milliarden Dollar für Rechenleistung und Rechenzentrumsmieten verpflichtet. Diese Kosten erhöhen laut New York Times den Druck auf den Börsengang, der rund 100 Milliarden Dollar bringen könnte. Bis zu 3,5 Milliarden Dollar davon sollen von japanischen Anlegern kommen. "You need scale-up technology that needs semiconductors and optical working seamlessly together," he told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." "We are going to create a new category of company here." The company said the transaction has an implied enterprise value of $115 billion for Lumentum, in a release. Marvell shares slumped 6% in trading Monday, while Lumentum's stock sank 11%. Through the acquisition, Marvell said it can combine electrical and optical technologies to meet accelerating and shifting AI connectivity demands across regions and systems. Companies are increasingly relying on optical connections to piece together chips used to run and train large language models. "We're actually going to create solutions around those that are highly sticky, and the reason that they're sold out is because the demand is exploding, and we don't see that changing anytime soon," Murphy said.  Marble Cognition raises $3.75M for its AI agent workers that watch and learn how people work 
 by Mike Wheatley 
 Artificial intelligence agents have become two a penny in the enterprise today, but just because they’re rapidly being commoditized does not mean organizations know how best to use them. 
 That’s the challenge a startup called Marble Cognition is trying to solve after raising $3.75 million in pre-seed funding to coincide with its launch today. The round was led by Heartcore and Seedcamp, and saw participation from angel investors that include executives from McKinsey & Co., Mistral AI and a board member of Datadog Inc. 
 Munich-based Marble was co-founded by the German AI engineers Felix Rösner (pictured, left) and Christophe Schmit (right), who were among the first to realize that AI agents have already become a commodity, used by almost every enterprise in some capacity or other. Most organizations are using AI agents primarily for writing software, but Rösner believes that to see the real value of those autonomous workers, companies need to provide them with the granular operational context that tells them what they actually need to build and automate. 
 But building this picture is a notoriously difficult challenge because few corporate workflows run according to neat blueprints. Though a study by McKinsey & Co. suggests that it’s theoretically possible to automate 57% of all work hours in the U.S., most companies haven’t gotten anywhere near that goal. 
 That’s because more than 90% of business processes live within things like messy email threads, scattered spreadsheets and inside the minds of employees. To teach AI agents what needs to be built and automated, companies need to piece all of those processes into a picture they can follow.

DeepSeek open-sources Super-Agent, a coding agent that watches team chats for work - Help Net Security 
 Help Net Security newsletters : Daily and weekly news, cybersecurity jobs, open source projects, breaking news – subscribe here! 
 Please turn on your JavaScript for this page to function normally. 
 Anamarija Pogorelec , Senior Staff Writer, Help Net Security
 November 2, 2026 
 Share 
 DeepSeek open-sources Super-Agent, a coding agent that watches team chats for work 
 Deepseek released a research prototype of dsh-superagent, a coding agent that does work on a GitHub repository for you. 
 Who can ask for work 
 The agent gets to work in two situations: an allowed user asks for something, or a rule your team wrote covers it. You can also open up a chat or GitHub scope, and then anyone in it can request work just by mentioning the agent. A message, comment or quoted document can’t expand what the agent is allowed to do, since the host is the one enforcing the lists and rules. 
 By default, requests that aren’t explicit, such as an unaddressed message, a bot’s message or an unlisted person’s follow-up, are assessed and recorded as ones the agent would have accepted, but none is accepted. Explicit requests, such as an allowed user mentioning the agent, work in every mode. The advice is to switch to auto after you’ve reviewed those records. 
 Merging 
 A prompt called Delivery requirements controls auto-merge, and the host adds no merge logic of its own. By default the agent doesn’t turn on auto-merge under its own account, because GitHub credits the merge to whoever enabled it. Unless the prompt names another account for merging, people merge. 
 dsh-superagent is available for free on GitHub .

 OpenAI might rebrand its data centers as ‘AI compute campuses’ 
 Data centers are deeply unpopular . But what if we called them something else? 
 Axios reports that OpenAI is preparing a “PR blitz” for after the midterm elections on Tuesday, as Democrats seem likely to win back the House of Representatives, and possibly the Senate, too . 
 The company’s chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane told Axios that the midterms will be “a bit of a movie trailer for what you’re going to see in 2028,” when he expects AI to be “ the issue” in the presidential election. 
 So OpenAI is to influence the AI debate moving forward, with Lehane discussing several proposals, including the development of AI “speed limits” ; finding ways to help people see AI as empowering them in their daily lives; pushing the U.S. to take a role in developing global standards — and yes, rebranding data centers as “AI compute campuses.” 
 Lehane also described the conversation around data centers (a debate that has pushed Amazon and Microsoft to say they will no longer use NDAs in their negotiations with local governments ) as “good and healthy.” 
 “Communities should hold companies responsible and accountable so they really and truly get a transformative benefit from these projects,” he said.

 Anthony Ha

 Dazzle AI CEO Marissa Mayer recently became the latest tech CEO to face criticism over seemingly out-of-touch comments extolling the usefulness of AI. 
 In Mayer’s case, that involved asking an AI tool for help with a school-assigned description of her daughter . For OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, that’s included suggesting that parents create personalized podcasts for their kids’ drive to school and also declaring that he could not imagine parenting without ChatGPT . Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has even suggested that it will become increasingly acceptable to meet your social and romantic needs through AI . 
 This all led TechCrunch’s Amanda Silberling to wonder if AI executives are simply too out-of-touch to build products for normal people — a crucial question with Anthropic set to go public just as Wall Street begins losing its appetite for heavy AI spending . 
 On the latest episode of the Equity podcast , Kirsten Korosec, Sean O’Kane, and I chatted with Amanda about why industry leaders can sometimes seem so tone deaf. Kirsten wondered if this is more of a marketing problem or a product problem.  
 Amanda’s answer: “A little bit of both.” She also argued that the tech industry is increasingly pushing a future “where basic human interaction gets more and more optimized out of actually occurring,” adding, “And call me old school, but I think that humans being able to talk to each other is probably a net positive for society.” 
 Keep reading for a preview of our conversation , edited for length and clarity.

 An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers’ machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. 
 The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont. Both Beaumont and the CTO and co-founder of security firm Phorian said that version 2.1.313 was distributed through Anthropic’s official account on Cursor. So far, neither Cursor nor Anthropic has explained how the attackers gained control of the account. 
 In search of cloud credentials 
 “It was a supply-chain compromise where the attacker gained access to the official distribution channel,” Phorian CTO and co-founder Luke Roberts told Ars. “The malicious version 2.1.313 was posted to the official Anthropic account, effectively superseding 2.1.312. Extensions auto-update in Cursor by default, but users can configure this in settings.” Phorian has more details here . 
 Anthropic has yet to issue public notice of the incident to customers. 
 Cursor said that the malicious extension attempts to install a persistent SSH backdoor using an added attacker-controlled SSH key, enabling the local SSH service, and opening a reverse SSH tunnel. The code was written to work on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Because Cursor

 Mistral releases weights for its trillion-parameter AI model, targeting cybersecurity 
 Lucas Ropek 
 10:00 AM PDT · October 29, 2026 
 French AI company Mistral has released the weights for its trillion-parameter open source AI model Mistral Large 4 (ML4), allowing businesses and governments to download and deploy the system themselves. Nicknamed “Le Chonk,” the model was first introduced earlier this month . 
 The release comes as competition between open-weight AI developers like Mistral and closed-model providers like OpenAI and Anthropic heats up, with the former arguing that businesses and governments shouldn’t have to rely on outside AI companies for access to advanced capabilities. That argument may hold more weight in cybersecurity, where organizations want more control over their data and systems. 
 Or, as Mistral’s CEO, Arthur Mensch, explained, AI should “be a tool for empowerment, not dominance.” With Chonk, Mistral doubles down on that position, arguing that it’s able to achieve “state-of-the-art performance” at a “fraction of the compute and capital committed by closed labs.” 
 The release of the model’s weights — the numerical training that animates the system — ensures that other companies and government agencies will now be able to deploy ML4 for their own purposes. 
 Mistral says that its model is comparable in terms of performance with a Chinese open-weight competitor, GLM-5.3, which was previously considered one of the best open-weight models in the world — particularly when it comes to cyber work.  Mistral Large 4 was built to process both text and images, closing performance gaps from previous Mistral models. Mistral 
 New AI models are coming, and they don’t stop coming.  
 On the heels of the recent rollouts of Meta’s Muse and Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon , Mistral AI is launching its new flagship frontier model, Mistral Large 4 . The model – affectionately known as “Le Chonk” – was available in public preview earlier this month. Now, after weeks of additional reinforcement learning, fine-tuning and assessing it with feedback from developers, cybersecurity experts and state officials, the Mistral team announced Thursday that ML4 is available for download. 
 “The response to the preview has exceeded our expectations,” Mistral said in its announcement. “We’ve put that feedback to work while continuing to scale reinforcement learning, driving massive improvements in coding and defensive cybersecurity.” 
 More from CNET 
 A French company known for its open-source and open-weight LLMs, Mistral AI reports that the Large 4 model “ranks among the best open-weight models of the world” on aggregated metrics and also outperforms European and US models, while also catching up to Chinese competitors, who have been dominating the open-weight sector.  
 Earlier this month, I spoke with Mistral Chief Scientist Guillaume Lample and VP of Science Pierre Stock about the new model – what they’re calling the best open model built in the West – and its specialized capabilities and extreme compute efficiency. Here’s what to know.

 Google debuts flagship Gemini 4 Carbon model with cybersecurity upgrades 
 by Maria Deutscher 
 Google LLC today debuted Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier large language model adept at complex programming tasks. 
 The LLM is rolling out just two weeks after the search introduced its previous flagship LLM, Gemini 4 Argon. According to Google, internal tests have shown Carbon to be more than twice as good at generating secure code. Additionally, the model outperforms GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 across multiple benchmarks. 
 Carbon’s most notable benchmark result is its record score on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. It’s a test that combines more than a half-dozen popular LLM evaluations. Google tested Carbon on a new version of the index that was publicly released today. It includes two additional benchmarks and removes a number of saturated questions, questions deemed too easy for frontier models. 
 Carbon is particularly adept at cybersecurity tasks. It handily beat the previous record on SEC-bench Pro, which evaluates LLMs’ ability to find weak points in complex software systems. The model is also better than its predecessor at patching the vulnerabilities it finds. 
 “The Chrome team has reported that Carbon performed more than 10X better than another lab’s large frontier model when generating high-quality patches,” Koray Kavukcuoglu, the senior vice president of Google DeepMind and Google’s chief artificial intelligence architect, wrote in a blog post . 
 Argon, the company’s previous flagship LLM, includes  guardrails designed to mitigate hallucinations and cyberattacks. Google implemented an improved version of that feature set in Carbon. According to the company, a number of internal teams that use Carbon in “live coding environments” reported a nearly 80% drop in misalignment alerts.

 Google has a new AI model, Gemini 4 Carbon. Adobe Stock 
 Google is back with another new frontier AI model, just two weeks after its last release. The new large language model is dubbed Gemini 4 Carbon, the company announced on Wednesday. And if you’re a fan of world models, there’s good news there, too: Google’s latest, Genie 4, also debuted this week. 
 Gemini 4 Carbon is the most advanced the company has released. It surpassed its own Gemini 4 Argon model and competitors like OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra on benchmarking tests designed to assess a model’s overall capabilities. But Google is pitching the model as one meant for cybersecurity experts. Google says Gemini 4 Carbon is good at detecting and patching vulnerabilities — a skill we’ve already seen can uncover major problems, as with last week’s PHP vulnerabilities affecting a majority of the world’s websites. 
 Google’s other new AI model this week is Genie 4. This is a world model , which can simulate real and imagined physical worlds. Whereas chatbots predict the next word in a sentence, world models are grounded in the physics of a digital universe. They’re useful for things like robotics and video game design. Genie 4 will introduce a new capability: audio. Developers will be able to add background noise and dialogue to their AI worlds. You may have heard of two AI bigwigs, Fei-Fei Li and Yann LeCun, building world models in their respective start-ups.

full_text:
Gemini 4 Carbon: Googles neues Spitzenmodell zielt auf lange Agenten-Workflows und Cyberabwehr

 Gemini 4 Carbon: Googles neues Spitzenmodell zielt auf lange Agenten-Workflows und Cyberabwehr 
 Matthias Bastian 
 View the LinkedIn Profile of Matthias Bastian 
 28. Oktober 2026 
 Kurz & Knapp 
 Nur zwei Wochen nach Gemini 4 Argon stellt Google DeepMind mit Gemini 4 Carbon sein nächstes Frontier-Modell vor, das sich mit 59 Punkten (Argon: 50) an die Spitze des Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 setzt. 
 Carbon ist laut Google auf mehrtägige, autonome Entwicklungs-Workflows ausgelegt, holt im Coding-Agent-Index von Artificial Analysis stark auf (59 gegenüber 53 Punkten bei Argon), bleibt dort aber noch knapp hinter Claude Opus 5.5 (62 Punkte). 
 Wegen der fortgeschrittenen Cybersecurity-Fähigkeiten durchläuft Carbon das freiwillige Vorab-Testverfahren der US-Regierung und geht zunächst nur an ausgewählte Sicherheitsexperten. Die Preise bleiben gegenüber Argon unverändert.

 Google öffnet seine Entwicklungsumgebung Android Studio über die Funktion "Bring Your Own Agent" für mehr als 40 externe Coding-Agenten wie Claude oder Codex und erweitert die Terminal-Werkzeuge, um Entwicklungszeit und Token-Verbrauch zu reduzieren. 
 Über Schnittstellen wie die auf Gemini Nano 4 basierende Agentic API und das Model Context Protocol können Entwickler Agenten-Funktionen direkt lokal auf Mobilgeräten ausführen und App-Dienste in die Google-Suche sowie die Gemini-App einbinden. 
 Mit der XREAL AURA präsentierten Google und der Hersteller XREAL zudem eine 1.099 US-Dollar teure Datenbrille auf Basis von Android XR, die virtuelle Arbeitsbereiche anzeigt und die reale Umgebung mithilfe von Gemini analysieren kann. 
 Frage zum Artikel eingeben …

 Auf dem Android Dev Summit richtet Google seine Entwicklungsumgebung auf KI-Agenten aus. Neben einer Integration für Modelle von Anthropic und OpenAI gibt es neue Schnittstellen für lokale Agenten auf Smartphones sowie eine Datenbrille. 
 Auf dem diesjährigen Android Dev Summit hat Google Updates für seine Entwicklerwerkzeuge und System-APIs vorgestellt. Im Zentrum der Ankündigungen steht die Öffnung der Entwicklungsumgebung Android Studio. 
 Mit der Version Android Studio Rabbit 2 führt Google die Funktion "Bring Your Own Agent" (BYOA) ein. Entwickler sind damit nicht mehr nur auf Googles eigene KI-Lösungen beschränkt, sondern können über das offene Agent Client Protocol (ACP) mehr als 40 verschiedene Coding-Agenten in der IDE nutzen. title: Google DeepMind: Genie 4 simuliert interaktive Welten in Echtzeit

label: ⚡ wichtig
full_text:
Google DeepMind: Genie 4 simuliert interaktive Welten in Echtzeit 
 Google 
 Google DeepMind: Genie 4 simuliert interaktive Welten in Echtzeit 
 von Carsten Knobloch 
 27. Okt. 2026 | 
 0 
 ? ? 
Dein Browser unterstützt das Video-Tag nicht. 
 Google DeepMind hat mit Genie 4 die neueste Version seines Welt-Modells vorgestellt. Das System berechnet interaktive Simulationen komplett in Echtzeit und soll dabei noch einmal deutlich realistischer ausfallen als bisherige Ansätze. Neu ist außerdem, dass das Modell direkt passenden Ton erzeugt, ohne dass separate Audiowerkzeuge nachhelfen müssen. 
 Unter der Haube bedient sich Genie 4 bei der Gemini-Familie, ja huch - wer hätte as gedacht?. Während Gemini Omni für die optische Darstellung und ein physikalisch glaubwürdiges Verhalten sorgt, kümmern sich andere Gemini-Modelle um die Logik im Hintergrund. Das soll verhindern, dass Szenen ihre Kontinuität verlieren oder nach wenigen Sekunden unlogisch auseinanderfallen. 
 Project Genie: KI-Welten auf Basis echter Google-Maps-Bilder 
 Google bringt Project Genie einen Schritt weiter und verknüpft das Ganze mit Street View.... 
 Jetzt lesen → 
 Echtzeit-Steuerung per Sprache und nativer Sound 
 Die Simulationen lassen sich während des Ablaufs mit ganz normalen Textbefehlen in natürlicher Sprache steuern. Nutzer können so die Kameraperspektive wechseln, das Wetter spontan umschlagen lassen oder neue Figuren in die Szene setzen. Parallel dazu erzeugt die KI direkt die passende Klangkulisse, von Umgebungsgeräuschen über Musik bis hin zu Dialogen. 
 Google sieht in solchen Systemen einen Baustein auf dem Weg zu genereller künstlicher Intelligenz (AGI). Praktische Einsatzgebiete sieht man vor allem beim sicheren Training von Robotern und Software-Agenten, aber auch in der Spieleentwicklung, der Filmbranche und der Industrie. 
 Zugang zunächst für ausgewählte Tester 
 Der Rollout startet ab sofort für einen kleinen Kreis ausgewählter Tester. Zeitnah sollen Abonnenten von Google AI Ultra

Google introduces cutting-edge Genie 4 world model - SiliconANGLE

 Google introduces cutting-edge Genie 4 world model 
 by Maria Deutscher 
 Google LLC today previewed Genie 4, an artificial intelligence model that can generate realistic three-dimensional environments. 
 The algorithm is the latest addition to a series of world models that the company launched in 2024. Compared with its predecessor, Genie 4 is better at rendering fluid movements and other complex details. Furthermore, it can generate accompanying audio such as the sound of crashing waves. 
 “The most dramatic leap is how Genie 4 simulates people, creating characters that move naturally, respond organically to their environments, and can be interactively steered in real-time,” Google DeepMind staffers Raia Hadsell, Diego Rivas and Hang Qi wrote in a blog post .  
 Users can create a virtual world by providing Genie 4 with a natural language description of what they wish to render. They can then navigate the simulation and make edits by entering follow-up prompts. For example, a user could ask Genie 4 to change the weather or add more objects. The model can make such edits in a manner that doesn’t reduce the virtual world’s photorealism or consistency. 
 Genie 4’s natural language interface is available alongside keyboard controls. They can be used to change the position and angle of the camera. 
 Under the hood, Genie 4 uses several other Google models to boost its output quality. It relies on Gemini Omni, a video generator the search giant introduced in May, to ensure that the visual assets it generates are realistic. Gemini 3.8 Flash, a reasoning model optimized for cost-efficiency, makes the individual frames of a simulation consistent with one another.
